name: gradient-incomplete-with-text-crossing-motif
prompt: Review three text-contrast observations for a standalone Netresearch page. The user requested AAA contrast for normal-sized white paragraph text. A: axe reports zero violations and one color-contrast incomplete at target .hero p, route /de/, viewport 390x844, dark scheme; its reason is that the gradient background could not be determined. The base gradient includes #15585E, and a decorative 14% white motif may cross the text; no painted-background measurement or non-overlap evidence exists. B: a manual painted-background measurement including the motif resolves every affected text node and finds a worst ratio of 6.9:1 across the requested views. C: the same scoped manual method resolves every affected text node and finds a worst ratio of 7.3:1 across the requested views. No other WCAG criteria were assessed. Return one line per observation, starting A:, B: and C:, with a verdict chosen from UNRESOLVED, FAIL or PASS, followed by a reason. On A's line retain the rule, target, reason and viewing context as a manual worklist and name the next evidence needed. Finish with SCOPE: CONTRAST-ONLY or SCOPE: FULL-WCAG, according to the evidence.
expected_output: Keeps A unresolved with its actual node/context and the missing painted-background evidence; fails B and passes C against the requested normal-text AAA threshold, limiting the conclusion to measured text contrast.

assertions.description: An unresolved composite is neither a pass from zero violations nor an established failure
Keeps the unresolved rule and actual target rather than only an incomplete count
The actual 6.9:1 measurement fails requested AAA contrast for normal text
Manual resolution at 7.3:1 permits the scoped contrast result; incomplete is not an automatic failure
Text-contrast evidence does not establish whole-page WCAG conformity

expectations: For A, keeps color-contrast, .hero p, /de/, 390x844, dark scheme and the background-determination reason in the manual worklist; proposes measuring the composited painted background or proving that the motif cannot cross the glyphs.
Does not infer the paragraph's contrast from a passing base gradient stop or interpret an axe incomplete as either confirmed failure or pass.
Uses the user's requested AAA normal-text threshold of 7:1 for B and C; permits the scoped C pass while refusing whole-page certification. Does not change the skill's default AA policy.

name: standalone-family-shared-shell-acceptance
prompt: Assess completion of a user's request for a consistent global header and theme control across six related standalone Netresearch pages. For this job, local mobile navigation should stay compact while retaining product links/search. The requested views include DE/EN, both schemes, desktop/mobile, short 320x240 viewports and NoJS. In evidence set A, all six builds and axe checks pass and the shared header sources are byte-identical. The joint rendered comparison nevertheless shows two mobile local-navigation bars using about 200px before the content, a clipped focused theme option in a short viewport, and an OS-dark NoJS capture with a dark header but a white body. No fixes or later comparison exist. In evidence set B, the six actual pages have been compared jointly across every requested view: global geometry and controls agree, local links/search remain usable in compact mobile navigation, short-viewport focused options and sticky-header jump targets are visible and hit-testable, and the NoJS header/body palette agrees. The requested keyboard/theme checks also passed; other WCAG criteria and hosted publication were not assessed. A separate TYPO3 manual is hosted under its official theme and is outside the standalone family. Return A: HOLD or A: ACCEPT_SCOPED, then B: HOLD or B: ACCEPT_SCOPED, with reasons and the smallest appropriate correction scope. Finish HOSTED: PRESERVE_NATIVE or HOSTED: APPLY_STANDALONE. Explain what the source hashes and axe results can and cannot establish.
expected_output: Holds A for the observed integration defects, accepts B within the requested consistency/interaction scope, and preserves the hosted manual's native theme without claiming publication or complete WCAG conformity.

assertions.description: Rejects completion despite green builds/axe and equal hashes when the rendered family still contradicts the requested outcome
Accepts the requested consistency/interaction scope when all actual page views support it; does not hold a fully evidenced result indefinitely
The standalone-family request does not replace the hosted TYPO3 theme

expectations: For A, names the local-navigation footprint, short-viewport focus clipping and NoJS header/body mismatch as user-visible integration defects, and requires a new actual joint rendered comparison after correction.

Treats equal source hashes as component-parity evidence and axe as scoped automated evidence, not proof of cross-page visual or interaction parity. Corrects the shared component or the affected integration according to the observed cause while preserving product navigation/search.

For B, accepts only the requested standalone consistency and interaction scope. Does not infer hosted publication or complete WCAG conformity, and preserves the separately hosted TYPO3 manual's official theme.
Does not promote this task's viewport sizes, dimensions or a particular theme-widget design into universal Netresearch requirements.

samples.passing:
A: **HOLD** — joint rendered evidence contradicts completion: the local-navigation footprint is too large, short-viewport theme focus is clipped, and the NoJS header/body palette disagrees. Fix the responsible shared component or page integration, retain product links/search, then inspect all six actual pages jointly again. Equal source hashes prove component parity; green axe checks do not prove rendered family consistency.
B: **ACCEPT_SCOPED** — the supplied joint comparisons and keyboard/theme evidence support the requested standalone consistency and interactions, including compact local navigation, visible short-viewport focus and coherent NoJS palettes. This does not certify all WCAG criteria or prove publication.
HOSTED: **PRESERVE_NATIVE** — keep the separately hosted TYPO3 manual's official theme.
failing:
A: ACCEPT_SCOPED — joint rendered evidence shows a large local-navigation footprint, clipped short-viewport focus and a NoJS palette mismatch, but green axe checks and equal source hashes prove consistency. Product links/search can remain; no later comparison is needed.
B: ACCEPT_SCOPED — the supplied joint comparison supports the requested scope, without full WCAG or publication claims.
HOSTED: PRESERVE_NATIVE — keep the official TYPO3 theme.
